Definition: , a reduplicated and prolonged form of πράω; (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses) contracted from περάω (to traverse; from the base of G4008); to traffic (by travelling), i.e. dispose of as merchandise or into slavery (literally or figuratively):--sell.
BiblicalUsage: Piprasko means to sell, to dispose of as merchandise. The merchant sold all he had for one pearl of great price in Matthew 13:46, and the first believers sold their possessions and shared with all in Acts 2:45. But Paul says the deepest sale of all in Romans 7:14: I am carnal, sold under sin. And Judas's friends counted the ointment's price in John 12:5, and missed its worth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe everything is sold to something — sin, or the kingdom. The merchant got it right: sell all for the pearl, because the pearl is worth more than all.
